methods.label: Use vertex form and symmetric root spacing
methods.explanation:
Vertex form makes the vertex condition easy to use and displays the symmetry of each pair of intercepts. Write
\[
f(x)=a(x-h)^2+v,\qquad a\ne0.
\]
Its vertex is \((h,v)\), and the given relationship gives
\[
g(x)=-a\bigl(x-(100-h)\bigr)^2-v.
\]
Because \((h,v)\) lies on the graph of \(g\),
\[
v=-a(100-2h)^2-v,
\]
so
\[
v=-2a(h-50)^2.
\]
Let \(d=|h-50|\). If \(d=0\), both graphs have their only intercept at \(x=50\), contradicting the positive inner gap. Thus \(d>0\).

Setting either quadratic equal to zero now shows that its roots lie \(\sqrt2d\) on either side of its vertex's horizontal coordinate. Those two horizontal coordinates are \(50-d\) and \(50+d\). Since \(\sqrt2>1\), the four intercepts, in increasing order, are
\[
\begin{aligned}
x_1&=50-(\sqrt2+1)d,\\
x_2&=50-(\sqrt2-1)d,\\
x_3&=50+(\sqrt2-1)d,\\
x_4&=50+(\sqrt2+1)d.
\end{aligned}
\]
This ordering covers either sign of \(h-50\), and it does not depend on the sign of \(a\).

The inner gap therefore gives \(2(\sqrt2-1)d=150\). Comparing the outer and inner gaps eliminates \(d\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
x_4-x_1
&=150\frac{\sqrt2+1}{\sqrt2-1}\\
&=150(\sqrt2+1)^2\\
&=450+300\sqrt2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The denominator is positive, so the division is valid. Since \(2\) is squarefree, \(m=450\), \(n=300\), and \(p=2\). Thus \(m+n+p=\boxed{752}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
